title: CompleteP for RL: Maintaining Feature Learning When Scaling Deep Reinforcement Learning
claim: Rich parameterization keeps optimal learning rates stable and features consistent across scale, yielding better compute and reward efficiency than the lazy baseline.
layout: 4 panels, 2x2 grid; top learning-rate sweeps side by side, bottom CKA and compute curves
description: A 2x2 grid of line plots. The top row has two reward-versus-learning-rate (eta, log axis) panels, titled CompleteP and NTK. Curves for widths N=64, 256 and 1024 are drawn in red-to-purple, and depths L=2, 4 and 8 use solid, dashed and dotted lines, with shaded bands for variance. In the CompleteP panel the reward peaks line up at about 10^-2 across widths. In the NTK panel the peaks shift as width grows. The bottom left panel is CheetahRun, L=5. It plots CKA feature similarity against checkpoint for widths 128 to 2048 in viridis colors, with solid lines for CompleteP and dashed lines for NTK. The bottom right panel is G1JoystickRoughTerrain, L=2. It plots reward against compute in FLOPs for widths 4 to 8192, again in viridis colors. The CompleteP curves are solid and the NTK curves are dashed. The eye goes first to the top two panels, where the optimum aligns in one panel and drifts in the other.
caption: CompleteP parameterization affords learning rate
abstract: The maximal update parameterization ($\mu P$) provides an approach to scale parameters while preserving feature learning in deep neural networks. In fixed data distribution settings it has been found to yield more stable learning dynamics, more consistent learned features, and enable optimal hyperparameters such as learning rate to transfer from small models to larger ones. However, it is unclear if these benefits readily transfer to reinforcement learning problems, where learning dynamics are coupled to the non-stationary data distribution induced by an agent's own actions. We empirically study how two regimes, the ''rich'' CompleteP and ''lazy'' Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) parameterizations affect hyperparameter transfer, feature and policy consistency, and learning behavior as we scale reinforcement learning agents. Ultimately, we show that agents trained using CompleteP consequentially improves compute and reward efficiency compared to the NTK parameterization across multiple control tasks and variants.
